recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If OO later wants to model multiple transfers, receiving organizations, custody events, or the identity of each receiving organization, that should be handled as a new tracker rather than further application of FHIR-23012.
issue_request: FHIR-23012 was a Published FHIR-core Specimen change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked which receiver counts for Specimen.receivedTime when specimens may pass through multiple systems or labs, and the approved resolution was to clarify the definition as receipt by the testing laboratory for processing.
initial_application: Jira records application to build with c851b6a13ef0ec37c373b20765947671140c7dd5. That commit changed source/specimen/structuredefinition-Specimen.xml from generic receipt for processing to receipt by the testing laboratory, and current blame still attributes the receivedTime short and definition wording to that commit.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists specimen=Specimen, so source/specimen/structuredefinition-Specimen.xml is in current core build scope. Broader Jira search found no later core tracker reversing the clarification. Later Zulip and Confluence hits show implementer and work-group discussion about custody/ownership and identifying the receiving lab, but no final conflicting decision for this issue.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The authoritative source already says "The time when specimen is received by the testing laboratory" and "Time when specimen is received by the testing laboratory for processing or testing.", which preserves the approved clarification.
